author: NorthEast News Desk
body: OpenAI is expanding its artificial-intelligence services into chip design, life sciences and financial services as it seeks more specialized enterprise work, Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar said Tuesday.

Reuters reported that OpenAI used its own models while developing a chip project called Jalapeno, which reached the tape-out stage in nine months. Tape-out marks the point when a finalized design is sent for manufacturing; it does not mean the chip is already in mass production.

Friar said the company is emphasizing outcome-based tools that can be measured against customer costs and productivity. She also described enterprise revenue as growing faster than overall annualized revenue during the latest reported monthly period.

The chip-design example points to a broader shift from general-purpose assistants toward systems embedded in technical workflows. Performance, security and the cost of checking model output will be central for companies deciding whether to use AI in design work where errors can be expensive. OpenAI did not disclose manufacturing yield, benchmark results or a commercial release date for the chip-design service.
dek: The company says its models helped move an internal chip project to tape-out in nine months as it pursues enterprise work beyond general chat.
headline: OpenAI expands AI tools into chip design and specialized industries
